13.0.s.en: (1) The sanctification of the firstborn and the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread

13.0.0.en: God commanded Moses to teach the people the sanctification of the firstborn son and likewise the firstborn of the beast. These had been killed among the Egyptians by the destroying angel, but the firstborn of God's people were redeemed by the Passover lamb, which is a symbol of Christ, and He purchased them with His blood, so they belong to Him; therefore He asks that they be set apart for Him.

13.0.1.en: The following is to be noted in the offering of the firstborn:

13.0.2.en: 1- Every firstborn was redeemed by the payment of five shekels of silver.

13.0.3.en: 2- The tribe of the Levites was a redemption for the firstborn of the children of Israel.

13.0.4.en: 3- The firstborn of the children of Israel exceeded the tribe of the Levites by 273 souls, so the redemption of each one was five shekels of silver (Num 3:39-51).

13.0.5.en: 4- The firstborn of clean animals are sacrificed to God, while unclean animals are redeemed with a lamb or have their necks broken (vv. 2, 12, 16).

13.0.6.en: 5- The firstborn remains seven days, nourished by its mother's milk, and then is sacrificed.

13.0.7.en: 6- The owner of the animal takes nothing from these firstborn, such as their wool, nor does he use them for work, but they are offered to God.

13.0.8.en: 7- It is not permitted to vow the firstborn of animals, for they will necessarily be offered according to the Law.

13.0.9.en: Set apart for God the beginning of your day, your best times and your abilities, in addition to offering the firstfruits of your possessions; and if God chooses one of your children for consecration, encourage him.

13.1.0.en: He reminded them of the day of their departure from Egypt, in which they had been enslaved for more than four hundred years (430 years). It signifies the bondage of sin, since Egypt was full of idols. So He asks them to be committed to eating unleavened bread, which signifies purity, and to reject leaven, which signifies evil, and to sanctify the firstborn and eat the Passover lamb.

13.1.1.en: When you repent and confess, be more careful to reject the sources of evil, remembering the humiliation of sin, so that you may keep away from everything that leads to it.

13.2.0.en: He reminds them to be committed to the feasts of Passover and Unleavened Bread throughout their lives, not only in the wilderness but also after they settle in the Promised Land and the pagan peoples are around them, so that they do not care for their foreign ideas but hold fast to the Law of God.

13.2.1.en: It is understood that the month of Nisan is the month of Abib. The month of Abib was the seventh of the months of the year, but God made it the first month, as mentioned in (ch. 12:2). Thus the Hebrews came to have a civil year, by which political, civil and agricultural matters were reckoned, and another, religious year, which begins with the month of Abib and by which feasts and religious occasions are reckoned. There is a month in the present Coptic year called Abib, but it is different from the month of Abib that existed among the Hebrews. The month of Abib corresponded to the present months of March and April; that is, the departure of the children of Israel was in the spring, which is a suitable time for their journey out of Egypt in the desert.

13.3.0.en: He affirms the commitment to eating unleavened bread for seven days and the removal of leaven, which signifies evil... The number "7" signifies the perfection of the work of the Holy Spirit; that is, we live our whole life in purity, keeping away from evil.

13.4.0.en: "A sign on your hand": that is, you do it with care.

13.4.1.en: "A memorial between your eyes": you understand it, remember it and see it always, so that you may fulfill it.

13.4.2.en: "In your mouth": you teach your children by it.

13.4.3.en: He stresses to him the commitment to observing the Passover and Unleavened Bread throughout his life, and teaching their spiritual meanings to his children through the generations.

13.4.4.en: Take care to teach your children and loved ones the spiritual teachings, so that they love God and the Church and are bound to Him, and ignorance does not hinder them from God, but the sweetness of fellowship with God is shown, directly or indirectly, according to the circumstances around you.

13.5.0.en: He reminds them to fulfill the law of offering the firstborn to God throughout their lives, when they go out of Egypt and then settle in the land of Canaan, and He commands them as follows:

13.5.1.en: 1- Offering the firstborn of man (the opener of the womb), the male, to God by consecrating him to Him. This is what happened in the consecration of the tribe of Levi for the service of God instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel (Num 3:11).

13.5.2.en: 2- The firstborn of man is redeemed by offering five holy shekels of silver for each firstborn, which is equal to about 75 grams of silver (Num 18:16), and this was before the males of the tribe of the Levites, who became instead of the firstborn of the children of Israel, were counted.

13.5.3.en: 3- Offering the firstborn of the male animal to God as a sacrifice.

13.5.4.en: 4- Unclean animals, such as the donkey, are redeemed by offering a lamb in place of their firstborn, and if it is not offered, the firstborn of the unclean animal is killed so that no one eats it. The Law that Moses received made clear the unclean animals and the clean animals, and it is understood from this, as we mentioned in the Book of Genesis, that clean and unclean animals were known before the Law of Moses; that is, the fathers had learned them from God.

13.5.5.en: 5- The male is offered because he represents strength, for we offer to God the best we have, in addition to the fact that he signifies Christ, who is the firstborn among many brethren (Rom 8:29).

13.6.0.en: He stresses the importance of teaching the children God's care and His power, which brought His people out with a strong hand from the bondage of Egypt after the killing of their firstborn. The means of their deliverance was the sacrifice of the lamb for the redemption of the firstborn; therefore they redeem the firstborn of man and offer the firstborn of the animals to God. And they place the words of this Law in phylacteries, that is, pieces of leather or cloth fastened on the forehead and wrapped around the head, and they also fasten another on the hand at the forearm. The intention is that they think about this Law and act by it, for the head signifies thought and the hand signifies action.

13.7.0.en: God did not lead them north to the land of Palestine, that is, the Promised Land, but they went from Rameses, which is near the land of Goshen, to Succoth, and then from Succoth they went south toward the Red Sea. Succoth is on the road between present-day Ismailia and Suez (map 2, p. 93). God made them wander far from the Promised Land because He knew their spiritual weakness: if they faced war they would be afraid and return to the bondage of Egypt. Therefore He allowed them to wander in the wilderness so that their only reliance would be on God. There was a short road leading north to Arish and Rafah, taking about two weeks to reach Palestine, but they would not have been able to face war with the Canaanites because of the weakness of their faith at that time. When they had spent forty years in the wilderness, their faith grew and they were trained in spiritual striving, so they were able to enter the Promised Land and face the Canaanites.

13.7.1.en: Kill the afflictions that pass over you, for they may be the solution for the salvation of your soul; God knows your nature and keeps you away from evil by using some afflictions.

13.8.0.en: Joseph felt his estrangement in Egypt despite his great position, and that his bones must be buried in the Promised Land, which is a symbol of the heavenly Jerusalem. So Moses remembered Joseph's command and took his bones with him as he left Egypt, and most likely he also took the bones of Joseph's brothers and carried them to Shechem in Canaan (Acts 7:16).

13.8.1.en: It is good that you always remember the estrangement of the world, so that you think of the beauty of eternity and strive to attain it, and so care for your readings, your prayers and your repentance.

13.9.0.en: The son and Israel moved from Succoth to Etham, on the edge of the wilderness of Sinai and on its border (map 2, p. 93). Thus they were left without a helper, and God then showed His care for them and sent them a pillar of cloud that covered them over their heads and protected them from the scorching sun throughout the day. It moved ahead above them, and as they lifted their heads toward it, they walked behind it.

13.9.1.en: It is a symbol of Baptism, because the cloud is a quantity of water like the water of Baptism, which gives those baptized in it a new nature, guides them to life with God, and passes with them through the afflictions that the scorching sun represents.

13.9.2.en: And at night the pillar of cloud turned into a pillar of fire from earth to heaven, moving before them, lighting their way, frightening their enemies and protecting them.

13.9.3.en: Darkness signifies sin and spiritual blindness, which the pillar of fire removes, lighting for them the way of life with God. It is of fire because our God is a consuming fire, and the pillar of fire signifies His commandments, which guide us to life with Him. Let us therefore be cleansed from every sin so that we may be pleasing before Him, and be assured of His power, which protects us from our enemies, the demons.

13.9.4.en: The pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire remained with them throughout the days of the wilderness; so God guides us and protects us throughout our life in the wilderness of the world.

13.9.5.en: Put God before you from the beginning of every day, so that your heart may be at peace and you may fear Him, and so reject sin, meditate on His love and enjoy fellowship with Him.

13.9.6.en: The crossing of the Red Sea

14.0.s.en: (1) God changes the direction of the children of Israel

14.0.0.en: "Pi Hahiroth": it means a farm, and perhaps Pharaoh had a farm there. It is located near the Gulf of Suez.

14.0.1.en: "Migdol": it means a tower or a fortress, and perhaps Egypt had a garrison in it to defend it against enemies. It is located near the Gulf of Suez.

14.0.2.en: "Baal Zephon": it means Baal of watching, and perhaps there was a temple there for the god Baal. It is located west of Suez on the Red Sea.

14.0.3.en: "By the sea": that is, by the Red Sea, at the point from which they crossed the sea.

14.0.4.en: God commanded Moses that they should turn toward the south, and the pillar of cloud moved to lead the children of Israel not eastward toward the wilderness of Sinai but south, beside the Bitter Lakes, toward the Gulf of Suez. They reached a place beside the Gulf of Suez, that is, before the sea near present-day Suez, most likely about ten miles south of Suez, and the width of the sea there is about eight miles. This distance is enough to hold all the people of Israel and then the army of the Egyptians after them.

14.1.0.en: "The wilderness hath shut them in": they became hemmed in in a dry desert, not knowing where to go, as if they were in a building that had been shut upon them.

14.1.1.en: News of the movements of the children of Israel will reach Pharaoh through his spies, and he will learn of the change of their course and think that they are bewildered.

14.2.0.en: "I will harden Pharaoh's heart": God uses Pharaoh's pride, so that the king hardens his heart.

14.2.1.en: Pharaoh and his army will pursue the children of Israel to bring them back to Egypt to serve him, and so the glory of God will be shown in the victory over him.

14.2.2.en: Do not be troubled by the increasing power of the wicked, for it is temporary, and God will give you victory in the end, because their power is nothing before God. God is long-suffering toward them, that perhaps they may repent, and so that your faith may be established and you may receive more abundant blessings.

14.3.s.en: (2) Pharaoh regrets letting the children of Israel go

14.3.0.en: After the departure of the children of Israel, Pharaoh felt his loss at the disappearance of this great number of workers in his service, and he regretted letting them go. Indeed he wanted to bring them back, and his servants and counselors encouraged him in this.

14.4.0.en: Pharaoh set out with his war chariot and the men of his army to bring back the children of Israel.

14.5.0.en: "Captains over every one of them" (literally, his charioteer soldiers): the soldiers trained to ride in war chariots and to fight the enemies from them.

14.5.1.en: "Chariot": a vehicle of iron and wood drawn by horses, in which the soldiers ride, so that they can run swiftly. Pharaoh took with him 600 war chariots, the soldiers trained to drive them, and a great army that was distinguished from the armies of the surrounding countries in the whole world.

14.5.2.en: The number (6) points to the whole perfection of human work, and the number (100) points to the perfection of the work of the community; that is, (600) means the utmost strength of man, especially since Pharaoh was the strongest of the kings of the earth at that time.

14.5.3.en: It is noted that some of the horses had died in the plague of hail while others lived, because those of the Egyptians who feared God had hidden their cattle, in addition to the purchase of other horses from the neighboring countries to replace what was lost, so that their armies would be complete and ready for war.

14.6.0.en: Pharaoh hurried with his army toward the children of Israel and overtook them while they were before the Red Sea, south of Suez.

14.6.1.en: If you have kept away from sin, do not return to it through the hardness of your heart, lest this be your last opportunity and you perish in sin.

14.7.s.en: (3) The terror of the children of Israel

14.7.0.en: When the children of Israel saw the greatness of the Egyptian army, they were very afraid, so they prayed to God with all their hearts, crying out that He would rescue them from this death or bondage.

14.8.0.en: The children of Israel murmured against Moses because they felt that their destruction before the Egyptians was certain, since they saw the sea before them and the armies of the Egyptians behind them. They were convinced that their death was certain, and they rebuked Moses for not leaving them in the bondage of the Egyptians.

14.8.1.en: Do not yield to sin, however difficult it may seem; it is better for you to die while striving than to yield to it.

14.9.0.en: Moses reassured them that the Lord would fight for them and defeat the Egyptians, and their threats and fear would vanish. He said all this by faith; perhaps God had informed him that he would triumph and be saved from the hand of the Egyptians, who would die, and that no harm would touch him and his people, so he believed the word of God.

14.9.1.en: By faith you can see what others do not see, and so you live in peace.

14.10.s.en: (4) The parting of the Red Sea

14.10.0.en: Moses prayed in silence and God heard him; indeed He counted his deep, quiet prayer as a cry, so He reassured him and asked him to bring the people near to the sea.

14.11.0.en: He commanded him to strike the sea with the rod so that it would divide into two halves and the children of Israel would cross on dry ground in the midst of the sea.

14.12.0.en: He told him of the hardness of Pharaoh's heart, who would not benefit from the miracle of the parting of the sea but would pursue the children of Israel even into the sea. He told him this to reassure him when he saw Pharaoh pursuing them inside the sea, and He commanded him to wait for the power of God, which would triumph over him.

14.13.0.en: God's purpose is not only to save His people but also the faith of the Egyptians when they see the defeat of their king and his army and their death.

14.14.0.en: It is declared here that the pillar of cloud or the pillar of fire is an angel of God who protects His people. The cloud used to cover the children of Israel to protect them from the heat of the sun, and now it turned into a pillar from earth to heaven separating the people of God from the Egyptians to protect them, so that the Egyptians could not see the people of God because of the mist. This was for the protection of the people of God and a warning to the Egyptians, that they might believe and turn back from pursuing the children of Israel. It is understood from this that the parting of the Red Sea took place in the daytime before the sun set.

14.14.1.en: Learn from God's warnings, so that you do not persist in your sin but return by repentance, and He will save you.

14.15.0.en: "The one to the other": the Egyptians to the children of Israel.

14.15.1.en: The pillar of cloud continued to separate the children of Israel from the Egyptians, and when night fell it turned into a pillar of fire, so the Egyptians were afraid and could not approach or harm the children of Israel.

14.16.s.en: (5) The crossing of the sea by the children of Israel

14.16.0.en: Moses struck the sea with the rod, and it divided into two halves by a strong east wind, and the bed of the sea appeared as dry land.

14.16.1.en: The rod signifies the Cross, which opens a way for you in the midst of the world, that is, the sea, so that you walk in peace.

14.17.0.en: The children of Israel advanced and walked on the ground, with the water like a wall to them on the right and on the left. They trusted in God who protected them, so they were not afraid of the water that stood miraculously like a wall on both sides of them.

14.18.0.en: Because of Pharaoh's hardness, he pursued the children of Israel into the sea and did not repent or learn anything from the miracle. The distance over which the children of Israel walked in the divided sea was about seven miles, at a place south of Suez. This long distance allowed about 2 million people to cross in it, followed by a great, mighty army of the Egyptians.

14.19.0.en: "The morning watch": that is, the time of daybreak, which is the end of the night, because the children of Israel crossed the Red Sea throughout the night, and at its end the pillar of fire moved and drew near to Pharaoh's horses and chariots. The horses were afraid and did not want to advance, so they drove them forward with great difficulty.

14.19.1.en: "Looked unto the host of the Egyptians": God looked upon them and troubled them with the pillar of fire that drew near to them, and they were very afraid.

14.19.2.en: "Took off their chariot wheels": the wheels of his strong iron chariots came off, because of the horses drawing back and the soldiers striking them to advance, so the chariots swayed and some of their wheels came off.

14.19.3.en: When God saw the hardness of Pharaoh's heart, He moved the pillar of fire toward his horsemen and chariots, and his strongest horses were afraid, and some of the army began to feel the power of God that protects His people, so they tried to flee and draw back. But Pharaoh's orders were strict to continue the attack and keep pursuing the children of Israel, and this was the last opportunity God gave them for repentance. It is noted that the Egyptians felt that the God of Israel was very strong and was fighting for His people, so they were troubled, but unfortunately they did not believe with the faith that calls to repentance and turning back; rather, their faith was like the faith of the demons in God, that is, they were insisting on their sin, so they perished. Even if they tried to flee, it was out of panic and fear, but they did not truly believe in God.

14.19.4.en: Repentance in words is not enough, but it must be carried out with swift striving, because your negligence will bring disgrace upon you.

14.20.0.en: After the children of Israel had come out of the sea and were in the wilderness, while the whole army of the Egyptians was inside the sea and the pillar of fire was still before them inside the sea, separating them from the children of Israel, God commanded Moses to strike the sea with his rod so that it would return as it was, and it covered the whole army of the Egyptians, and all of them died.

14.21.0.en: The children of Israel had crossed the sea walking on dry ground and then came out of the sea into the wilderness of Sinai.

14.22.0.en: In the morning the children of Israel found themselves safe in the wilderness, and then the sea cast up many of the bodies of the Egyptians on the shore, because all of them had died; some of their bodies were on the bottom and some were thrown by the waves onto the shore.

14.23.0.en: Before the mighty power of God, the faith of His people in Him was established, and they submitted to their great leader in faith, Moses.

14.23.1.en: Look at God's works with you and meditate on them, so that your faith in Him may be established and you may submit to His commandments. The Tasbeha (praise) and going to Marah and Elim
